articles.title: Zelensky Urges US to End Month-Long Patriot Missile Delay as Russian Strikes Kill Civilians
articles.body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky urged the US on Tuesday, Oct. 27, to approve urgently needed Patriot interceptor deliveries that have been delayed for nearly a month, warning that shortages are leaving Ukrainian civilians vulnerable to deadly Russian ballistic missile strikes.
His appeal followed Russian attacks on Kyiv on Monday evening and overnight that killed a 46-year-old woman and injured 15 others. The strikes damaged the State University of Trade and Economics, including student dormitories and academic buildings, as well as nearby Kyoto Park, residential buildings and transport infrastructure. Five of those injured were university students and staff, Ukrainian officials said.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“It’s important that the world sees this, that our partners see it in the US, on which almost everything concerning Patriots depends,” Zelensky said in his evening address, calling for the necessary Pentagon authorizations to deliver the interceptors.
The president warned that delays in Western air defense assistance were making it increasingly difficult for Ukraine to protect its cities.
“Everyone hears and sees that it is now difficult for us to defend against Russian ballistic missiles. Above all, we lack missiles for Patriots,” Zelensky said.
He said Russia had launched more than 100 ballistic missiles against Kyiv and the surrounding region in the two weeks since Oct. 14.
Ukraine Holds Its Strongest Frontline Position in a Long Time, Zelensky Says
A day earlier, on Oct. 26, Zelensky revealed that Ukraine had been waiting nearly a month for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to authorize deliveries of missiles for Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems.
“In particular, we have been waiting for nearly a month for Mr. Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS,” Zelensky said, adding that he had instructed Ukrainian officials to raise the matter with Washington again.
The delay reportedly affects missiles already paid for by Ukraine’s allies.
Some of Ukraine’s interceptor supplies are purchased through NATO’s Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL), under which European allies and other partners finance American-made weapons for Kyiv.
Because the missiles are manufactured in the US, transfers from partner countries can require American authorization.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio previously acknowledged that a batch of interceptors might not have arrived but said the delay was not politically motivated.
The Pentagon has maintained that US policy on military assistance to Ukraine has not changed, while emphasizing the need to preserve sufficient American interceptor stocks.
For Kyiv, however, the delay comes as Russian ballistic missile attacks continue to cause civilian casualties and damage critical infrastructure.
“Every support package is an opportunity to protect people’s lives,” Zelensky said Monday.
Ukraine seeks Patriot interceptors from other partners
With US authorization still pending, Ukraine is pursuing additional interceptor supplies from European countries and other partners.
Zelensky said Monday that Ukrainian officials were working through several channels to secure PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles, both used by Patriot air defense systems.
“We are working on several tracks – with the US, Europe, and other partners that have stocks of PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles,” he said.
“Conversations with other countries are also ongoing.”
The president said preparations were underway for the next meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group, known as the Ramstein format, expected in November.
You can also highlight the text and press Ctrl + Enter

articles.title: Poland to Host €227M Patriot Missile Service Center
articles.body:
Poland has announced that it will be hosting a European service center for US-made PAC-3 interceptor missiles, aiming to cut repair times for weapons that are already in short supply worldwide and critical to Ukraine’s defense against Russian ballistic missile attacks.
Polish Deputy Defense Minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, who led Warsaw’s negotiations, called the decision “historic” in a statement on Tuesday, Oct. 27. Three other countries had competed to host the facility, she said, naming Germany, the Netherlands and Norway.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“This success was not a given. It is the result of many months of negotiations and the hard work of the entire team,” Sobkowiak-Czarnecka wrote, noting that the Polish bid had been the highest rated since the application stage.
According to TVP World citing Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, the hub would be the only one of its kind outside the United States. Its cost would be roughly 1 billion Polish zlotys (about $253 million) and would take about a year to become fully operational.
In her statement, the defense minister thanked Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, who appointed her chief negotiator.
The outcome showed what was possible when the government and the country’s President Karol Nawrocki pulled in the same direction, she added.
POW Dispute: South Korea Pulls 8 Diplomats From Ukraine
Short repair times for scarce interceptors
PAC-3 missiles, used in US-made Patriot air-defense systems, are currently shipped to the US for servicing, which led Washington to seek a European site to cut turnaround times, TVP World reported.
The US, Poland, Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden signed an agreement with manufacturer Lockheed Martin in July, in an aim to explore setting up such a hub.
According to the broadcaster, Warsaw has long pursued the project with hopes that it would eventually lead to Patriot missile production in Poland.
Plant near Warsaw seen as likely site
Although the government did not officially name a location at the time of the report, TVP World reported that the WZE electronics plant in Zielonka, located about 15 kilometers (9.3 miles) northeast of Warsaw, is widely seen as the leading candidate.
In September, Sobkowiak-Czarnecka toured the plant with US Under Secretary of State Thomas DiNanno. At the time, the US Embassy in Warsaw noted that the visit highlighted bilateral cooperation on critical Patriot components.
Under a 2019 agreement with Lockheed Martin, the plant already produces and services key PAC-3 MSE components, TVP World reported.
Ukraine facing critical shortage
As of Oct. 15, Ukraine has reportedly depleted its stocks of Patriot interceptor missiles.
For the country, the PAC-3 is currently among the very few weapons capable of intercepting Russia’s Iskander-M, a ballistic missile carrying a half-ton warhead strong enough to tear down a quarter to half of a typical apartment block.
The shortfall was particularly felt during Russia’s large-scale attack overnight into Wednesday, Oct. 14, when most incoming ballistic missiles reached their targets. The strike hit three power plants in Kyiv and energy facilities in Kharkiv, killing four people and injuring at least 25 in the capital.
According to CNN’s exclusive, Ukraine fired its last remaining Patriots as the Air Force shot down four Russian ballistic missiles during that same attack.
Around the same time, the US aerospace giant Starlink tweaked parameters and limited terminals above 160 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour), crippling Kyiv’s drone operations, including interceptor drones used against Russian jet-powered Shahed drones.
As of Oct. 1, Lockheed Martin is in advanced talks over PAC-3 production outside the US over tripled demand, as countries seek to rebuild their stocks amid the war in Iran and Russia’s escalating rhetoric towards Europe.
For much of the year, Ukraine has repeatedly appealed to its Western partners for faster deliveries of Patriot interceptors.
On Sept. 8, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said Germany would deliver PAC-2 missiles to Ukraine from it’s own Bundeswehr stocks, while Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara said contracts are being signed with partners for about 1,000 Patriot missiles.
During the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York, US President Donald Trump said he made a “final decision” to grant Ukraine the licenses to produce Patriot missiles domestically, after backtracking on the previous July commitment.

articles.title: F-16 Jets to Add Startup Castelion’s Hypersonic ‘Blackbeard’ Missile
articles.body:
The Air Force has awarded Castelion, a venture capital-backed defense startup founded in 2022, a contract to integrate its hypersonic Blackbeard missile onto the F-16 Fighting Falcon.
The announcement, which came from the company via social media on Oct. 26, marks a major advancement in the Air Force’s work on hypersonic munitions.
Neither the Air Force Research Laboratory, which awarded the contract, nor Castelion immediately responded to a request for comment.
The same day, the service awarded a $694 million contract to Lockheed Martin, a longtime defense prime, to begin production of the hypersonic Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported.
The Blackbeard missile has drawn strong interest across the Pentagon, with the Navy pushing to field the rocket-powered, boost-glide strike weapon with a nearly 500-mile strike range on the sea service’s F/A-18 Super Hornet.
Navy Development
The Navy’s Air Test and Evaluation Squadron 23 used the Super Hornet to conduct carriage and separation tests of Blackbeard on Sept. 18 at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Md., which validated the weapon’s compatibility and flightworthiness on the aircraft.
The service selected Blackbeard as the winner in its Multimission Affordable Capacity Effector program, which shifted it to a program of record under framework contract orders of up to $200 million.
The company won a $105 million contract to integrate the missile on the F/A-18 Super Hornet in April.
The MACE initiative sought an affordable hypersonic missile about the size of an AIM-120 AMRAAM air-to-air missile.
In June, the service awarded the company its first production contract, worth $23.4 million, for 50 early operational capability pre-production prototype Blackbeard missiles.
Subsequent delivery orders from the Navy aim to speed up Blackbeard pre-production prototypes to EOC status and field the low-cost hypersonic weapon.
USAF Spending and Development
For its part, the Air Force has spent nearly $21 million to date on Blackbeard research and development, and AFRL added $16.4 million in a September contract modification for the missile.
Those dollars cover development through June 2028 under current spending and contractual agreements.
The USAF contract modification also pursues compatibility with the F-35A.
While the F-35 is the services’ main fifth-generation tactical fighter, the F-16, like the Navy’s workhorse Super Hornet, are workhorse fourth-gen fighters that can carry more munitions without worrying about compromising stealthy characteristics.
The Air Force has more than 600 F-16s in the fleet and recently moved forward with plans to upgrade the decades-old software system for those crucial aircraft, Air & Space Forces Magazine previously reported.
The Big Picture
The Air Force now has a three-pronged approach to hypersonic munitions.
These include Castelion’s Blackbeard, an air-to-air missile; the Lockheed Martin AGM-183A ARRW, a strategic strike-focused, exquisite, long-range hypersonic missile; and the Raytheon/Northrop Grumman Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile, a cruise missile option to strike ground or maritime targets.
ARRW successfully completed booster and All-Up-Round tests and is poised to add terminal seeker and data-link integration for moving-target tracking in its Increment 2 tests. The strategic strike missile is envisioned for the B-52 Stratofortress and B-1B Lancer.
The AHM-4A HACM is built for internal or external carriage and geared for both fighter and bomber use to add high-volume magazine depth to the fleet. The missile achieved milestone flight tests over an undisclosed Australian range in late September, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported. Initial operational delivery of HACMs is slated for 2027.
Additionally, AFRL recently posted a request for white papers on developing a more advanced hypersonic rocket engine for its current and future munitions dubbed the Rotating Detonation Rocket Engine.
If successful, the more affordable, mass-produced engine could extend ranges, increase speed, and up the payload for future hypersonic, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported.

articles.title: U.S. Air Force puts its first hypersonic missile into production
articles.body:
- The U.S. Air Force awarded Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract to produce and field the ARRW hypersonic missile.
- The service withheld quantities and delivery dates, three years after it had planned to cancel the weapon without production buys.
The U.S. Air Force has put its first hypersonic weapon into production, awarding Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract on Sept. 29 to build and field the AGM-183A Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, or ARRW, a missile the service had planned to abandon just three years ago, the Department of the Air Force announced on Oct. 26.
The service withheld how many missiles the contract covers and when deliveries will begin, citing operational security, but said the award formally moves the weapon out of prototyping and flight testing and into production. The contract was placed through the Department of War’s Enterprise-Wide Agile Acquisition Contract.
ARRW is a boost-glide weapon that rides a solid-fuel rocket booster to more than five times the speed of sound, about 6,100 km/h (3,800 mph), before releasing a glide vehicle that maneuvers toward its target, which makes it far harder to track and intercept than a conventional ballistic missile. The U.S. Air Force says it will let aircraft strike time-sensitive, heavily defended and high-value targets from long range, outside the reach of enemy air defenses.
“This is a turning point in our advanced weapons roadmap. By moving ARRW from test to production, we’re providing our combatant commanders with a credible, high-speed strike weapon capable of penetrating the most advanced anti-access and area-denial systems,” said Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink.
The missile is too large for most fighters and will initially be carried by the B-52 Stratofortress bomber, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported, and it has also reportedly been tested on the B-1.
“Fielding ARRW enhances our ability to hold targets at risk anywhere around the world. This hypersonic weapon provides the Joint Force a flexible and rapid response option for highly contested environments,” said Chief of Staff of the Air Force Gen. Ken Wilsbach.
The production decision caps a troubled development history. Lockheed won the design contract in 2018, but the first three flight tests starting in 2021 failed before the missile flew successfully in May 2022, and in March 2023 the service’s then top acquisition official, Andrew Hunter, said the program would end without any production buys as the U.S. Air Force shifted its focus to the smaller Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile. The service reversed course in 2025, when then-Chief of Staff Gen. David Allvin told Congress the U.S. Air Force would buy ARRW.
The program received $362 million in fiscal 2026, and the U.S. Air Force has requested $452 million for production in fiscal 2027, although that request is stalled in Congress while the Pentagon operates under a continuing resolution at 2026 funding levels. Budget plans call for $556 million to $621 million a year for ARRW procurement from 2028 to 2031, with missile quantities marked as controlled unclassified information.

articles.title: Kiev makes new demand for European interceptors
articles.body:
Kiev makes new demand for European interceptors
Ukraine has asked five European nations to release 10% of their interceptor missile stockpiles to ease the shortage of air defense ammunition.
Defense Minister Evgeny Khmara presented the proposal by video on Monday to his counterparts from France, Germany, Italy, and the UK, and Polish Deputy Defense Minister Pawel Zalewski, who met in Paris. He said their Patriot and IRIS-T stocks can be replenished from future deliveries contracted for Ukraine with foreign funding.
Khmara floated a similar proposal for advance deliveries of Patriots last month. Kiev also accused Washington of delaying deliveries of the interceptors. US officials cited the competing military needs of their own forces and denied any change in policy toward Ukraine.
The five countries’ joint statement made no commitment to supply additional interceptors, though they reiterated their support for Ukraine “by all available means – politically, militarily and financially.”
Poland and the Netherlands have said they have no Patriot missiles to spare; Greece has warned that aid must not undermine its own defenses. Germany, a key donor, has pledged additional older PAC-2 interceptors from its military stocks. Other European countries have reportedly held back PAC-3 missiles to preserve their own reserves.
The shortage comes amid an escalating exchange of long-range strikes. Kiev intensified drone attacks on Russian oil refineries and retail warehouses over the summer in what Ukrainian leader Vladimir Zelensky called a “40-day pressure campaign.” Russia has said its increased strikes on Ukrainian targets are retaliation. Ukrainian forces are struggling to intercept Russian ballistic missiles and faster, jet-powered long-range drones.
Kiev is also seeking additional financial support after overspending this year. Zelensky has asked European donors for at least €70 billion ($78 billion) to cover military and budget needs; Western governments are struggling to agree on how to finance additional aid.
The EU, which borrowed €90 billion ($100 billion) last year to prop up the government in Kiev for 2026-2027, is facing tensions among member states, with the Czech Republic, Hungary, and Slovakia saying they won’t take part in a potential new loan proposed by the European Commission.

articles.title: Strategic partnership of Poland and Great Britain. Three-Year Defence Cooperation Plan signed.
articles.body:
Strategic partnership of Poland and Great Britain. Three-Year Defence Cooperation Plan signed.
27.10.2026
- The Polish-British alliance has never been as strong as it is today. The agreement we signed, increasing our capabilities and cooperation, is the best example of that. We have signed an agreement on the plan of cooperation in defence. This three-year plan is the result of the Polish-British treaty, signed a few months ago. I am very grateful for this plan of cooperation. It shows our joint involvement: Polish and British soldiers, joint exercises, developing skills. The most important capabilities we are working on are the new technologies, long-range precise strikes, Artificial Intelligence, drones, anti-drone measures, but exercises training our classic capabilities and cooperation in various conditions will be organized based on this defence plan which we have signed today - said the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz.
On 27 October 2026, a bilateral meeting took place in Warsaw between the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, and the Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting. The Deputy Minister of National Defence Paweł Zalewski also took part in the talks between the two delegations. The main part of the visit of the British delegation was the signing of the Three-Year Defence Cooperation Plan of the Republic of Poland and the United Kingdom by both ministers.
- Great Britain is an important partner for us when it comes to defence production. The Miecznik programme, whose phases proceed according to schedule, building integrated air defence – Narew, Pilica, Pilica+ programmes, creating an independent production line for 155 mm ammunition – these are just some of our joint initiatives. One of the largest allocations, or our investments in air defence, is being created in cooperation with Great Britain. The selection of submarines by Poland, and deciding on Sweden also happened in cooperation with Great Britain, who will have a large hand in this process. It was one of the most consequential decisions that we have undertaken.
- added the Deputy Prime Minister, noting the most important areas of cooperation.
- We have begun our meeting with the important topic of support for Ukraine. (…) This tyranny, this oppressive, neo-imperial policy of the Russian Federation is a source of harassment for Ukraine since 2014, since the occupation of Crimea and on to the full-scale invasion later. The response of Poland and Great Britain is unambiguous: we will defend liberty with all our might, we will defend our rights and our land, every centimetre of our territory. I believe I can say that during our vis-à-vis meeting the Secretary has proposed a very important message. Among the different international formats, and our ironclad alliances, we have a similar view of the alliance with the United States. Both Poland and Great Britain is in favour of strengthening this transatlantic alliance, and Great Britain is a great example of this – it is from Great Britain that all that is connected to the transatlantic alliance originated. We are in favour of strengthening and building our own capabilities, of greater independence of Europe, but not a disconnect with the United States.
- said the Minister of National Defence.
The signed document maps avenues of strategic cooperation between the Armed Forces of both countries until the end of the decade. The main topics of discussion were matters of adapting the military to hybrid threats, saturating the eastern flank of NATO with modern deterrence potential, as well as strengthening industrial ties. The ministers have also confirmed their unity and coordination in their efforts to support Ukraine.
- This is an important moment in bilateral relations between our countries. The ties of friendship and solidarity between the United Kingdom and Poland go deep, but this is not merely about our shared history – it’s also about our similar assessment of the threats we face today and our joint determination that in this struggle between liberty and tyranny the United Kingdom and Poland will not be passive bystanders. Thanks to the leadership of Poland, its experience and perspective, when Poland calls, the United Kingdom responds. We hear loud and clear what Poland experiences every day, what some call hybrid threats from Russia – I personally prefer to call it state-sponsored terrorism – I see the daily mobilization of your forces and air defence in the face of drone incursions. We are also seeing, not just in Poland but across NATO, how Putin is testing us and tests the determination of NATO. (…) The meaning of what we are doing here today is that it strengthens our capabilities, our defence industry potential and, critically, our alliance. (…) I am thankful for your friendship, support and solidarity. Poland is one of our greatest and, without a doubt, most reliable friends in Europe, and we cherish and nurture this friendship
- noted the British Secretary for Defence Wes Streeting.
>>> GALLERY – The meeting of the defence ministers of Poland and Great Britain

articles.title: Germany’s Helsing promises jet-drone-hunting missiles at under $100,000 a shot—its CEO doesn’t expect them on the market before 2027
articles.body:
German defense AI firm Helsing has unveiled Contra, an AI-run air defense system and two interceptor missiles designed to chase Russia’s jet-powered Geran drones, the company announced on 26 October. Officials pitch it as cheap, but it won’t reach the market this winter.
That leaves Ukraine on its own defenses as Russia shifts to jet drones. By early October, jet models made up about 40% of Russian drone launches, and Ukraine’s own interceptors for them won’t arrive in needed numbers before late November, Air Force Deputy Commander Yurii Cherevashenko said.
Two missiles, one AI brain
Contra is the command layer of air defense: it links radars and other sensors, tracks incoming drones and missiles, and assigns a weapon to each target, while people keep control over decisions, Helsing said. Besides the company’s own missiles, it can also use other firms’ interceptors, lasers, guns, or nets. AD-1 Inferno is jet-powered and designed to loiter, swarm, and re-engage targets, while AD-2 Ambush, a solid-fuel rocket, is designed to reach Mach 2.5, over twice the speed of sound, and a range of more than 20 km, the company said.
Inferno, with a 700 km/h speed and a 20-km range, would be the everyday shooter. Ambush would handle “leakers,” drones about to hit the ground, said Maxwell Adams, Helsing’s senior product director. Each shot should cost under $100,000, company officials said.
Built for the faster Gerans
Ukraine once downed 90% of Russia’s slower, propeller-driven Gerans, copies of Iran’s Shahed, Defense News reported. Russia has since fielded thousands of jet Geran-4s and Geran-5s flying at 400–700 km/h, and almost half now get through, Helsing co-founder and co-CEO Gundbert Scherf said.
Ukraine’s own nightly rates swing widely. On 28 September, President Zelenskyy put the shoot-down rate for jet drones at 57%. Overnight on 7 October, it exceeded 82%, National Security and Defense Council Secretary Ihor Klymenko said. Russian output of the two models has reached 4,000 a month, Helsing said, citing unspecified intelligence reports.
Helsing has signed one Contra contract, Scherf said, but the system is still in testing, and he expects it on the market in the second half of 2027. Ukraine already uses Helsing’s HX-2 strike drones. Scherf said they should be integrated into a system like Contra.
Read also
- Russia replaces Ukrainians with Russian settlers in occupied Kherson Oblast; only 10–20% of pre-war population remains, Ukraine says
- Finland and Norway leaders make rare direct call to Putin, breaking with the West’s diplomatic isolation of the Russian leader to influence Ukraine peace talks
- Oleshky ceasefire expands beyond occupied town as truce holds without reported violations

articles.title: German soldier led local branch of Putin-linked Night Wolves biker club for years, The Insider finds
articles.body:
A Bundeswehr serviceman spent several years leading the German branch of the Night Wolves motorcycle club, and he continues to hold a leadership position with the group. The Insider found a ruling by a German military disciplinary court dismissing the soldier from service. His name was withheld in the ruling, but The Insider identified him as Alexander Sautner, a dual German-Russian citizen. Sautner initially served as vice president of the club’s “Roads of Victory” division, where he was responsible for organizing international motorcycle rallies. In early 2023, Sautner became vice president of the independent German chapter of the biker club: Night Wolves MC Germania. Despite a disciplinary investigation against him, Sautner continued directing the club’s activities and maintaining contacts with its Russian leadership.
A Bundeswehr soldier
The German military court’s ruling describes in detail how a Bundeswehr serviceman came to hold a leadership position in the Night Wolves.
The soldier is not named in the document, but the charges list the actions that formed the basis of the case against him. They include his participation on April 11, 2022, in a Rossiya Segodnya video conference featuring a Soviet flag in the background, several links to RT and Sputnik material that he posted in 2015, and criticism of Polish authorities for refusing to allow a Night Wolves motorcycle convoy to cross their border. According to publicly available information, the only German participant in the aforementioned April 2022 news conference was Alexander Sautner, and the same posts cited in the ruling can be found on Sautner’s Facebook page (1, 2).
According to the court, Sautner was born in Kazakhstan, moved to Russia with his parents at the age of 2, and relocated with his family to Germany in 1994. He holds both Russian and German citizenship.
Sautner joined the Bundeswehr in July 2007 as a noncommissioned officer candidate and attended the German Air Force’s NCO school. After completing his training, he served in transport units, working in vehicle logistics. In February 2010, he was promoted to Stabsunteroffizier, a junior noncommissioned officer rank, and in January 2013 he was transferred to a logistics battalion.
From July to November 2013, Sautner took part in the International Security Assistance Force mission in Mazar-i-Sharif, Afghanistan, receiving the Bundeswehr’s bronze deployment medal for his service. He was also awarded the gold-level military service badge.
A September 2013 performance review described Sautner as an experienced, motivated, and results-oriented noncommissioned officer. His commanders praised his openness, honesty, good relations with fellow soldiers, and overall strong performance. In August 2018, at his own request, Sautner transferred to another unit within the logistics battalion.
Sautner’s Bundeswehr contract was not due to expire until June 30, 2032. However, even before the 2018 transfer, Sautner had begun participating in the activities of the Night Wolves motorcycle club — infamous for its longstanding ties to Vladimir Putin, including its role in Russia’s 2014 annexation of Crimea. According to Germany’s Military Counterintelligence Service, known by its German acronym MAD, Sautner had been a club member since around 2016 and had taken part in its motorcycle rallies even earlier than that.
Sautner later became the first German member of the Night Wolves to achieve “full color” status, meaning full membership in the motorcycle club. In biker culture, “colors” are patches bearing a club’s name and emblem that members wear on their vests. The right to wear the complete set signifies that a person has progressed from supporter and prospective member to a full member of the club.
Sautner later became vice president of the Roads of Victory division, replacing his wife’s uncle in the role. The court ruling does not specify exactly when that happened, but MAD describes him as a longtime vice president and says that until the spring or summer of 2022, he played a key role in organizing and running international motorcycle rallies.
Roads of Victory is a themed Night Wolves division that organizes annual motorcycle rallies around May 9, Russia’s Victory Day commemorating the defeat of Nazi Germany in World War II. Before an independent German chapter was established, Night Wolves activities in Germany were carried out through Roads of Victory, which was headed by Andrei Bobrovsky. Bobrovsky, for his part, is an associate of Night Wolves founder Alexander Zaldostanov, who came under European Union sanctions in 2022. As vice president, Sautner effectively headed Roads of Victory activities in Germany.
The Night Wolves motorcycle club itself was founded by Zaldostanov in 1989. MAD documents say the organization has about 45 chapters in different countries and operates under a strict hierarchy. According to the counterintelligence agency, members are required to follow the club leadership, while Zaldostanov can issue instructions directly to members of foreign chapters.
The Night Wolves and several of the club’s leaders are under EU sanctions for supporting Russia’s aggression against Ukraine. The sanctions justification says the organization spreads Russian propaganda, supports pro-Russian armed formations in Ukraine, and maintains close ties to the Kremlin.
German military counterintelligence regards the Night Wolves’ activities as one instrument of Russia’s hybrid warfare efforts against Germany. MAD assesses that the annual motorcycle rallies are used not only as commemorative events, but also to spread pro-Russian political messages.
How the investigation into Sautner began
The first suspicions among Bundeswehr commanders emerged in 2020, when Sautner’s battalion commander and a security officer noticed a Night Wolves emblem sticker on the rear window of Sautner’s car while it was parked on military premises. At the time, Sautner was working primarily as part of the Bundeswehr’s assistance to civilian health authorities. However, after his links to the Russian motorcycle club were discovered, his commanders concluded that he could no longer be assigned to perform work involving classified information.
Sautner’s former direct superior, whose name was withheld in the ruling, testified that the soldier was primarily assisting civilian health authorities at the time, but the restriction on deploying him to posts requiring security clearance created problems for a unit that had commitments to NATO’s rapid-response forces. The situation was compounded by Sautner’s military specialty, which was in short supply, making him difficult to replace.
Sautner also told the court about the circumstances that prevented him from passing the security vetting required for access to classified information, saying that he had retained Russian citizenship because renouncing it would have involved significant expense. He also refused to sign a pledge not to visit certain countries that were considered potential security risks. The ruling does not identify those countries. Holding a second citizenship is not itself prohibited for Bundeswehr service, and the court documents do not indicate that Sautner concealed the existence of his Russian passport from his commanders.
On Feb. 4, 2021, the Bundeswehr’s logistics command formally opened disciplinary proceedings against Sauter, and in December of that year, he was informed of the main findings, which centered on four Facebook posts he had made between 2015 and 2019. Sautner was offered the opportunity to respond, but declined.
On Jan. 27, 2015, Sauter commented on a Sputnik report about Ukrainian military losses in the Donetsk region, writing that Ukrainians could now try out their crematorium. Military disciplinary prosecutors interpreted the remark as incitement to violence and hatred.
On April 27, 2015, Sautner criticized Polish authorities for refusing to allow Night Wolves participants in a motorcycle rally to transit the country on their way to Berlin. He complained that the bikers were being prevented from honoring those killed in World War II and called the Polish authorities “dirty U.S. vassals.”
On Sept. 4, 2015, Sautner shared an article from the German magazine Compact describing the country as an occupied American colony. He posted another article, this time from RT Deutsch, on June 26, 2019. It concerned historical memory and relations between Russia and the West.
The Insider found the first two posts, which were described in detail in the court ruling, on Sautner’s Facebook page. The court ultimately did not consider the four posts in its final judgment, and they were not brought up during Sautner’s disciplinary hearing because they were unlikely to materially affect the type or severity of the punishment.
Notably, despite the investigation, Sautner continued participating in Night Wolves activities. On May 9, 2021, during one of the Roads of Victory rallies, he was seen carrying the flag of the self-proclaimed “Luhansk People’s Republic.” MAD assessed that displaying the symbol of the unrecognized Russian-backed statelet demonstrated how commemorative events were being used to promote Russian political messages.
Instructions from Night Wolves leaders and a pro-Russian demonstration in Berlin
After Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, German military counterintelligence uncovered evidence of direct interaction between Sautner and the club’s Russian leadership. MAD materials cited in the court ruling say Sautner maintained direct contact with Alexander Zaldostanov and Andrei Bobrovsky and received instructions from them, including while members of the club leadership were in the war zone in Ukraine.
One such episode occurred in early March 2022, mere days after the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion on February 24.
In club correspondence from March 4 and 5, counterintelligence officers found discussions of a demonstration in Berlin that was to be held under the stated aim of opposing alleged persecution of Russian-speaking residents of Germany. According to MAD, Sautner received a personal message containing instructions from Roads of Victory president Bobrovsky, who was referred to as Hauptkommandant, or “commander in chief” in the correspondence. Participants were urged to fight on the “information front.”
Sautner then sent a voice message to the German Roads of Victory group chat strongly urging other club members to attend. On March 5, 2022, Sautner appeared with other Night Wolves members at a demonstration at Berlin’s Brandenburg Gate, where he posed with a Russian flag bearing state symbols and the word “Russia.” Photographs from the event were later reviewed by the court.
Sautner said he attended the demonstration to protest discrimination against Russian-speaking people in Germany, adding that he was particularly concerned about his own children. The court, however, viewed the event as a public display of solidarity with Russia staged against the backdrop of the start of its invasion of Ukraine.
The court ruling also mentions another public appearance by Sautner. On April 11, 2022, he participated by video link in a news conference organized by the Russian state media group Rossiya Segodnya. A Soviet flag with a hammer and sickle was visible behind him. MAD interpreted the episode as a further demonstration of Sautner’s senior position within the Night Wolves leadership.
Raising money for Donbas
During the investigation, German military counterintelligence also examined messages from a WhatsApp group called NW DP GERMANY, which was found on Sautner’s phone.
One message asked club members to contribute 1,000 rubles (around $13 at the time) each by Feb. 1, 2022, and then another 500 rubles per month to support Night Wolves chapters in Donbas. The appeal was posted by Denis N., whom German counterintelligence described as a close confidant of Sautner. The person was Denis Nalyotov, who later became head of the club’s German branch.
MAD assessed that the collected funds could have been used to purchase equipment suitable for armed operations against Ukraine. On Feb. 27, 2022, after the full-scale invasion had begun, Sautner himself called on members of the German Roads of Victory organization to send 13 euros each to a person named Badja. According to the message, the money was intended for humanitarian aid to Donbas.
On March 1, Denis Nalyotov discussed the collection with another club member, Thorsten M. He said the money could be sent by PayPal but that it would be better to wait for an in-person meeting and hand it over in cash so the transfers would leave no record.
On April 26, Sautner said in a WhatsApp voice message that around 1,000 euros had been collected. He said the money had been transferred to a fund called “Humanitarian Aid for Donbas.”
MAD materials also cite correspondence from March 2, 2023, in which Badja again called for donations for humanitarian aid. A Roads of Victory representative in Germany replied that fundraising was already underway.
The court ruling does not establish that Sautner personally purchased military equipment or that the funds collected were in fact used for armed activity against Ukraine. The possible military purpose of the money appears specifically as an assessment by MAD.
How Sautner became vice president of Germany’s Night Wolves
In the spring or summer of 2022, Sautner stepped down as vice president of the German Roads of Victory organization, being replaced by Denis Nalyotov. Сounterintelligence assessed that Sautner may have given up the title because of pressure from German law enforcement. Disciplinary proceedings against him were already underway, and MAD documents also refer to an investigation by Germany’s Federal Prosecutor’s Office. The court ruling does not disclose details of that investigation.
The formal transfer of the post, however, did not mean Sautner stopped playing a leadership role. According to MAD, he continued coordinating all major decisions with Nalyotov, with the two generally making and implementing them together.
In early 2023, the Night Wolves established an independent German chapter, Night Wolves MC Germania. Nalyotov became president of the new organization, while Sautner became vice president.
The two informally divided Germany into two zones. Nalyotov ran the northern chapter from Hanover, while Sautner oversaw the south from Bad Mergentheim in Baden-Württemberg. Flight records reviewed by The Insider also indicate that Sautner and Nalyotov traveled to Moscow together after Russia launched its full-scale invasion. (Nalyotov flew from Kaliningrad to Moscow on Jan. 15, 2023, and returned on Jan. 21.)
Sautner therefore obtained a new formal leadership position in the Night Wolves’ German structure after the Bundeswehr’s disciplinary proceedings had already begun. MAD assessed that Sautner’s appointments as club president and vice president indicated a particularly high level of trust from Alexander Zaldostanov. MAD also found that the Russian leadership continued to control foreign chapters, including the organization of propaganda events in Germany.
At the court hearing, Sautner confirmed that he remained a full member of the Night Wolves and continued to serve as vice president of the German chapter.
Why Sautner was not dismissed from the Bundeswehr until 2026
On March 9, 2022, the proceedings were suspended pending additional disciplinary charges. The Bundeswehr’s Federal Office of Personnel Management later considered dismissing Sautner under a law allowing the expedited removal of soldiers involved in anti-constitutional activities without lengthy court proceedings. Sautner was temporarily suspended from official duties in April 2022, and the hearings continued for several more years. On May 26, 2025, the agency determined that there were insufficient grounds execute Sautner’s expedited removal, and the disciplinary case against him continued.
Then on Oct. 10, 2025, Sautner was served with an amended charge sheet. In addition to the earlier Facebook posts, the case now included three new allegations: participation in the pro-Russian demonstration on March 5, 2022; serving as vice president of the German Night Wolves chapter from at least early 2023 through July 29, 2025; and sending an insulting email to a fellow soldier.
The final incident occurred on April 19, 2025. During the night, Sautner emailed a senior NCO in his unit complaining that he had not been informed about the death of a former fellow serviceman. Sautner said the man had died by suicide and accused the command of inaction. The email contained numerous insults directed at members of the unit.
At the court hearing, Sautner apologized to the recipient. The court nevertheless found that he had deliberately violated his duty to treat fellow soldiers with respect.
The court also heard testimony from Sautner’s former commanders, who described him as an experienced, calm, and reliable soldier widely respected by his colleagues. One commander said he had been surprised by the allegations against him.
At the same time, Sautner’s former superiors said that given his actions, they no longer considered his return to the Bundeswehr possible. According to the court ruling, Sautner had openly discussed his Night Wolves activities on his Facebook page, meaning his links to the club were known within his unit.
When Sautner was asked during the hearing whether he even wanted to remain in the Bundeswehr, he was unable to answer immediately. Ultimately, the judges concluded that Sautner had deliberately violated his soldierly duties to remain loyal to Germany, to uphold its constitutional order, and to refrain from conduct that could undermine trust in the Bundeswehr. The court separately stressed that Sautner’s leadership role in an organization closely linked to the Russian state was incompatible with service in Germany’s armed forces.
The ruling also noted that Sautner did not end his Night Wolves activities after the investigation began. On the contrary, while disciplinary proceedings were already underway, he assumed an even more prominent position in the club. The court considered that to be an aggravating factor.
“He can no longer be the servant of two masters,” the ruling said. The judges were quoting wording used by Sautner’s own defense, although the document does not explain the context in which his lawyer used the phrase.
The judges ruled that the Bundeswehr’s trust in Sautner had been irreparably destroyed. On Jan. 28, 2026, Germany’s military disciplinary court found him guilty of disciplinary violations and ordered his dismissal from service. Sautner was also denied special transitional payments following his dismissal and ordered to pay court costs.
The judgment became final on Feb. 5, 2026. The decision was based on Sautner’s leadership role in an organization that German counterintelligence links to the Russian state, his public participation in a pro-Russian demonstration after the start of the full-scale invasion, and his violations of military duties.

articles.title: Russian Ballistic Missiles Hit Kyiv University Campus, Killing One and Injuring Nine
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
Russian Ballistic Missiles Hit Kyiv University Campus, Killing One and Injuring Nine
Editor’s note: this is a developing story.
UPD 2, 23:49 Kyiv time: The person killed was found in a partially collapsed three-story non-residential building in the Dniprovskyi district, according to the State Emergency Service. The injured were hurt at several locations in the Desnianskyi district, including the campus and dormitories.
UPD, 23:24 Kyiv time: One person has been killed and nine injured, most of them students living in a university dormitory, according to Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko.
Russian ballistic missiles struck the territory of a local university campus, Kyoto Park, areas adjacent to a metro station, and nearby residential quarters in Kyiv on the evening of October 26, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
He highlighted that the attack directly targeted densely populated civilian locations with no military facilities nearby.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Zelenskyy stressed that artificial delays in supplying air defense systems to Ukraine directly assist Russian terror when cities face persistent strikes.
He called on international partners to fulfill defense agreements without delay and to provide Ukraine with the necessary capabilities to strike Russian ballistic missile launch systems as the most effective method to save lives.
According to Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko, the Russian ballistic attack left one person dead and 9 others injured. Most of the victims were students residing in a university dormitory. Emergency medical services hospitalized nine of the wounded.
Among those caught in the attack was an emergency medical crew responding to a call near the Lisova metro station in the Desnianskyi district; a paramedic and an emergency medical technician suffered non-critical injuries.
The assault caused widespread destruction across the Desnianskyi and Dniprovskyi districts. In the Desnianskyi district, a missile landed near a university dormitory, shattering its windows and injuring a 20-year-old woman.
Blast waves also damaged a nearby residential building, where emergency crews suspect residents may be trapped under the rubble.
In the Dniprovskyi district, shockwaves blew out windows in the intensive care unit of one hospital and two departments of another facility, though no personnel or patients were injured. A separate strike hit a non-residential site near a local supermarket, killing one civilian.
On October 21, the United States restored critical early-warning intelligence sharing with Ukraine regarding Russian ballistic missile launches after a Russian strike hit a 24-story residential building in Kyiv's Sviatoshynskyi district.
The attack struck near the 20th floor, triggering a fire that killed two people and injured two others. Zelenskyy confirmed the resumption of intelligence cooperation following meetings with US officials, emphasizing that early warnings provided civilians with crucial time to seek shelter from incoming ballistic missiles.

articles.title: Houthis claim attack on Saudi oil refinery, blasts shake Riyadh
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Yemen's Houthis claim attack on Saudi oil refinery, blasts shake Riyadh
Yemen's Houthis said they targeted Saudi Arabia's biggest oil refinery with a ballistic missile on Tuesday, as blasts shook the capital of the world's top crude exporter.
Saudi Arabia, the Middle East's largest economy, has suffered weeks of strikes from the Iran-backed Houthis against oil and civilian sites including Riyadh's international airport.
"The Yemeni Armed Forces were able to target the Ras Tanura refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile," Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree posted on X, saying the strike caused "massive fires".
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis earlier said it had shot down three missiles fired by the group towards the Eastern Province.
A resident in the city of Al Khobar, south of the Ras Tanura complex, told AFP he heard explosions around dawn and received a text message alert.
"We got the alert on the mobile and then heard a very loud bang," the resident said.
Maritime security agency Vanguard said a fire was reported in the Ras Tanura area in the early hours of Tuesday after an attack.
"The fire has reportedly been contained, while the extent of damage and any impact on oil-loading operations remain unclear at current," Vanguard said.
The Ras Tanura facility along Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast is home to one of the largest refineries in the Middle East and a cornerstone of the kingdom's energy sector.
The complex has a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day. It has been repeatedly targeted by strikes blamed on Iran, including a drone attack in early March that forced a partial shutdown of the refinery.
Meanwhile a series of explosions echoed across the capital, Riyadh, shaking office windows in the city centre. A text message alert warned residents to seek shelter.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted two ballistic missiles that were fired at Riyadh.
Egypt 'declared war'
Earlier, a Houthi official said the Egyptian parliament's decision to authorise defensive military support for Saudi Arabia amounted to a declaration of war.
Egypt's parliament authorised the measure on Monday, following a request from Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.
"It is truly remarkable that while these people go to discuss what they call 'peace in the region', Egypt and its parliament declare support for the so-called defence of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and in doing so, declare war against the Republic of Yemen," said Mohammed Ali al-Houthi, a member of the Houthis' political bureau, in a Telegram post.
It was not clear exactly what support was on offer from Egypt, which has the Arab world's largest military.
Al-Houthi's statement also pointed to Monday's visit to Tehran by the Saudi defence minister, Pakistan's army chief and Turkey's intelligence chief, in a bid to de-escalate tensions in the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Riyadh, Ankara and Islamabad recently signed a NATO-style defence pact in Mecca, pledging to consider an attack on one country as an attack on all three.
Turkey and Pakistan have not announced any strikes on the Houthis during the group's weeks of attacks on Saudi Arabia.
'Not afraid of any alliance'
The Houthis said the group was "not afraid of any alliance that may be formed".
Yemen's largely dormant conflict reignited in July, further destabilising the region months into the Middle East war between the United States and Iran.
The Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before seizing swathes of Red Sea coastline in a major offensive in September.
The Houthis have in turn reported frequent Saudi strikes targeting areas under their control.
This month the Houthis ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, forcing the cancellation of flagship events and shutting down Riyadh's airport for two weeks.
The Houthis' war with the Saudi-led coalition began in 2015, months after they ousted the internationally recognised government from the capital Sanaa in September 2014.

articles.title: There were 16 ballistic missiles overnight — Zelenskyy on Russia's attack
articles.body:
There were 16 ballistic missiles overnight — Zelenskyy on Russia's attack
Kyiv • UNN
Zelenskyy reported that Russia attacked Ukraine with 16 missiles and more than 280 drones. There are hits, and 12 people injured in the strike on a university campus in Kyiv.
Russia launched 16 ballistic missiles at Ukraine overnight on October 27. President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported this while reacting to the enemy's overnight strike, UNN writes.
Consequences of Russia's strike on Kyiv
"The number of people injured after Russia's strike on the university campus and surrounding area yesterday evening has risen to 12, five of them students and university staff. While emergency services were helping people and dealing with the aftermath of the first strike, the Russians used ballistic missiles again," Zelenskyy said on social media.
What and where Russia attacked
A total of 16 ballistic missiles were launched this night. And more than 280 drones. Unfortunately, there are casualties and strikes in Kyiv, including on the Pivdennyi Bridge. This is a serious escalation in Russia's operation against our logistics. There were also strikes on Kyiv region, Vinnytsia region, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipropetrovsk region, Kharkiv region, Odesa region, Chernihiv region, Sumy region, Donetsk region, Kherson region and Chernivtsi region. Almost everywhere, Russia's targets are energy facilities, logistics and ordinary urban infrastructure
On Patriot and other air defense systems
"Artificial and prolonged delays in the supply of interceptor packages for Patriots and NASAMS, which have unfortunately occurred recently, are directly helping Russia achieve the goals of its terrorist campaign. Every such delay means another Russian strike hitting one facility or another. Unfortunately, strikes occur every day," the President said.
"Russia is constantly taking new escalatory steps. Pressure on Russia and real support for Ukraine are needed to change the situation. I thank everyone who truly supports our defense of life and understands the importance of support packages arriving on time. We must bring peace closer and save lives. Thank you to everyone who stands with Ukraine!" Zelenskyy emphasized.

articles.title: Ukraine Downs 2 Ballistic Missiles, 255 Russian Drones in Overnight Attack Targeting Kyiv
articles.body:
Ukrainian air defenses shot down or neutralized two Russian ballistic missiles and 255 drones during an overnight attack primarily targeting Kyiv, the Air Force reported on Tuesday, Oct. 27.
Russia launched the attack from 6 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 26, using Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles from Russia’s Bryansk region and 280 strike drones, including Shahed-type unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), Gerbera drones, and Parodiya decoys.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Of the Shahed-type drones, 69 were jet-powered, according to the report on Telegram.
As of 9 a.m. on Tuesday, Ukrainian forces had intercepted or suppressed 257 aerial targets: two ballistic missiles Iskander-M/S-400 type and 255 drones. These included 56 jet-powered Shahed-type UAVs.
Several strike drones remained in the air, and combat operations were ongoing at the time of the report.
Air Force said impacts from Russian aerial weapons were recorded at 25 locations, while debris from intercepted targets fell at 16 locations.
Separately, the State Emergency Service (DSNS) reported that Russian forces carried out more than 40 attacks across five districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region overnight, injuring three people in the Synelnykove district.
Fires broke out in a multi-story residential building, vehicles, private homes and outbuildings. Residential houses also caught fire in the Nikopol and Pavlohrad districts.
In the city of Dnipro and the Kamianske district, infrastructure was damaged and a fire broke out. Rescuers extinguished all the fires, the DSNS reported.
Molodist Film Festival Marks 55 Years, Bringing International Cinema to Kyiv Oct. 24-Nov. 1
Russian strikes on Kyiv overnight into Tuesday, prompted the closure of the South (Pivdennyi) Bridge, a major crossing connecting the capital’s eastern and western banks of the Dnipro River.
Kyiv Mayor Vitalii Klitschko released the first photos showing damage to the bridge as specialists assessed the extent of the damage.
The Kyiv City Military Administration (KMVA) also reported disruptions on the Green (Syretsko-Pecherska) metro line, with trains operating separately between Syrets and Vydubychi stations and between Osokorky and Chervonyi Khutir stations.
The bridge remains closed to traffic, and authorities have not announced when it will reopen or when normal metro service will resume. The crossing carries both road traffic and part of the Green Line.
In a separate development, Russian ballistic missile strikes damaged an administrative building in Kyiv’s Podilskyi district and non-residential buildings at two other locations.
The attack followed Monday evening strikes on a university campus and nearby residential areas that killed one person and injured over 10 others, most of them students.

articles.title: Russia Halts Fire Near Ukraine's Oleshky for Aid Mission, Immediately Strikes Kyiv
articles.body:
A localized ceasefire between Ukrainian and Russian forces took effect at 3 a.m. Kyiv time on October 27 in and around Russian-occupied Oleshky in Ukraine’s Kherson Oblast to allow a humanitarian mission, Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and Russia’s Defense Ministry said.
Lubinets announced the start of the truce on Telegram, saying the parties were honoring agreements reached with Russia’s human rights commissioner, Yana Lantratova, who heads the Russian negotiating team. The Russian Defense Ministry confirmed that its forces had halted fire on the Kherson front and introduced a “silence regime” from 4 a.m. Moscow time.
The ceasefire is part of a humanitarian operation being organized by Ukraine in cooperation with Lantratova, with mediation and coordination from U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. Lubinets said he would continue providing updates while prioritizing the safety of Oleshky’s civilians and compliance with the agreed arrangements.
The White House said Trump had secured the truce after meeting with U.N. officials who briefed her on the situation in the town. She said civilian officials from Russia and Ukraine would visit residents in their homes to “determine the level of assistance they require.” Residents wishing to evacuate would receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination, she said, adding that some might choose Russia and others Ukraine.
The Ukrainian and Russian General Staffs had previously announced that a ceasefire would begin in a designated area during the night of October 27 to enable the humanitarian operation. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed that Russia had agreed to the truce, while Lubinets said the mission would take place soon.
The pause in fighting is intended to allow humanitarian aid and civilian evacuations from Oleshky, where up to 2,000 people are stranded with dwindling supplies of food and medicine, according to the U.N. The town has been under Russian occupation since the early days of the full-scale invasion and lies across the Dnipro River from Kherson.
Russian forces have effectively blockaded Oleshky, preventing humanitarian aid from entering. Residents face severe shortages of food, water and electricity, while mined roads and persistent drone attacks make evacuation extremely dangerous. Civilians attempting to escape along the only roads in and out of the town are frequently targeted by drones.
The truce comes as the worsening humanitarian crisis in Oleshky has attracted international attention, including from Pope Leo XIV. The aid mission is planned ahead of another round of U.S.-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine expected next month, aimed at ending more than four and a half years of war.
Newsmax, a right-wing U.S. cable network, said it had received “exclusive television access” to accompany observers entering the town on Thursday.
Minutes after the ceasefire began, Russian forces launched a wave of ballistic missile strikes against other parts of Ukraine, including Kyiv. Multiple explosions shook the capital shortly after 3 a.m., while air raid alerts sounded across several parts of the country.
Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said a Russian strike damaged the Southern Bridge across the Dnipro River, including its metro infrastructure. City officials said train services over the bridge had been suspended.
The capital had also come under attack late Monday, when Russian ballistic missiles struck the grounds of a university, killing one person and injuring 10, according to city officials.
Klitschko reported damage to medical facilities in the capital, saying a blast wave shattered windows in an intensive care unit. Windows were also broken in two wards at another medical facility in the same district, but no patients or medical staff were injured, he said on social media.
A building in a nonresidential area was also hit, with one person reported dead near a supermarket, according to Klitschko. A separate strike near a university dormitory shattered windows and injured a 20-year-old woman.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russian ballistic missiles hit a university campus and surrounding areas, including Kyoto Park, the area near a metro station and residential buildings.
“The missiles hit very crowded areas, and there is not a single military facility nearby. This was a strike directly on the city, on its infrastructure,” Zelensky said on social media.
In Kharkiv, Ukraine’s second-largest city, Russian attacks late Monday killed two people and injured four.
“It is important that the world sees that Russia is showing nothing but a desire to kill and continue waging war,” Zelensky wrote in an online post.

articles.title: Zelensky after Russian strike on Kyiv: Delays in air defense support Ukraine enable terrorism
articles.body:
Zelensky after Russian strike on Kyiv: Delays in air defense support Ukraine enable terrorism
Volodymyr Zelensky made this statement on Telegram, according to Ukrinform.
“Russian ballistic missiles struck the grounds of one of Kyiv’s universities and the surrounding area—essentially the campus, Kyoto Park, the area near the metro station, and residential buildings. It is not yet known exactly how many people were affected. But, unfortunately, there are casualties. There are wounded. Rescue operations are ongoing. There is extensive damage, and there are reports that people may be trapped under the rubble,” he wrote, noting that all relevant emergency services on the ground are doing their job—rescuing people.
Zelensky emphasized that the missiles struck in very crowded areas where there are no military facilities nearby—this was simply an attack on the city and its infrastructure.
Unfortunately, the head of state warned, there may be repeat strikes.
“And it is precisely under such conditions—when the threat is constant, when strikes can occur at any moment and target cities and villages—that artificial delays by air defense forces only aid the terrorists,” the President stated.
He noted that it is important for political agreements to be promptly implemented at the operational level. It is also important for partners to understand that Ukraine needs the proper tools to destroy Russian ballistic missile launchers. According to Zelensky, this would be the most effective way to save lives.
“It is important for the world to see that Russia demonstrates nothing but a desire to kill and continue the war. Ukraine must not be left to face this alone, and it is entirely Russia’s fault that the war is still ongoing and people are still dying. Please, take care of yourselves. All partners should stand with Ukraine in protecting lives,” the President of Ukraine concluded.
As reported, on the evening of October 26, Russian troops launched a ballistic missile strike on Kyiv. As of 11:24 p.m., one person was reported dead and ten wounded.
Photo: Office of the President

articles.title: Zelensky on overnight attack: Russia targeted energy, logistics, and urban infrastructure almost everywhere
articles.body:
Zelensky on overnight attack: Russia targeted energy, logistics, and urban infrastructure almost everywhere
According to Ukrinform, the head of state said this in a Facebook post.
“Artificial and prolonged delays in deliveries of interceptors for Patriot and NASAMS systems, which have unfortunately been occurring recently, directly help Russia achieve the objectives of its terrorist campaign. Each such delay results in another Russian strike hitting a target. Unfortunately, attacks occur daily. Russia is constantly taking new escalatory steps. Pressure on Russia and tangible support for Ukraine are needed to change the situation,” Zelensky said.
He noted that the number of people injured in a Russian strike on a university campus and the surrounding area the previous evening had risen to 12, five of them students or university staff.
“While emergency services were helping people and dealing with the aftermath of the first strike, the Russians launched another ballistic missile attack. A total of 16 ballistic missiles were launched overnight, along with more than 280 drones. Unfortunately, there have been casualties, and targets in Kyiv were hit, including the Southern Bridge. This is a serious escalation in Russia’s campaign targeting our logistics,” the President said.
He added that strikes had also targeted the Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv, Odesa, Chernihiv, Sumy, Donetsk, and Kherson regions, as well as Chernivtsi region. In almost every region, Zelensky said, Russia’s targets were energy facilities, logistics, and civilian urban infrastructure.
As Ukrinform previously reported, President Volodymyr Zelensky said the previous day that Ukraine had been waiting for almost a month for U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth to sign off on the supply of missiles for Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems.
Photo: State Emergency Service of Ukraine

articles.title: Kyiv’s South Bridge Hit as Russian Ballistic Missiles and 280 Drones Hammer the Capital
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
Kyiv’s South Bridge Hit as Russian Ballistic Missiles and 280 Drones Hammer the Capital
Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv’s South Bridge during a massive overnight assault that also sent 280 drones toward Ukraine, forcing the bridge to close and disrupting metro service across part of the capital.
Russia launched a massive overnight attack against Ukraine, sending 280 drones—including 69 jet-powered Shaheds—along with ballistic missiles, with Kyiv identified as the main target.
The strike damaged the capital’s South Bridge, forcing authorities to close it to traffic and suspend metro service across part of the city, according to Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko on October 27.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Klitschko said specialists were inspecting the South Bridge to determine the extent of the damage following the Russian attack.
Traffic across the bridge has been completely suspended while the assessment is underway.
The strike also disrupted Kyiv’s Green Line metro service, with trains temporarily halted between Osokorky and Chervonyi Khutir stations. Authorities have not yet said when either the bridge or the affected section of the metro will reopen.
Klitschko also released the first photographs showing damage to the bridge following the attack.
Russia is increasingly targeting Kyiv’s seven bridges across the Dnipro River in an effort to divide the Ukrainian capital and disrupt transport connections across northern Ukraine.
Disrupting crossings over the Dnipro could effectively split the city in two, with consequences extending far beyond the capital.
According to Ukraine’s military, Russia launched Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles from Russia’s Bryansk region as well as 280 strike and decoy drones from multiple locations in Russia, the occupied Donetsk region, and occupied Crimea.
The drone force included Shaheds, Gerberas, Parodiya decoys, and other types. Sixty-nine of the Shaheds were jet-powered variants. Kyiv was the primary target of the attack.
Ukrainian fighter aircraft, surface-to-air missile units, electronic warfare teams, drone units, and mobile fire groups were all involved in repelling the strike.
By 9 am, Ukrainian air defenses had shot down or suppressed 257 aerial targets, including two Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles and 255 drones.
Among the intercepted UAVs were 56 jet-powered Shaheds.
Several attack drones were still airborne when the preliminary figures were released, and air-defense operations remained underway.
Ukraine reported Russian strikes at 25 locations, while debris from intercepted targets fell at another 16 sites.
This is not the first Russian strike on one of Kyiv’s bridges. Previously, a Russian Shahed drone struck Kyiv’s South Bridge as a metro train crossed.
Passengers reported hearing an explosion and seeing a flash as the drone hit near the roadway. Smoke then appeared inside the carriage, ash entered through the ventilation system, and several windows were blown out.
Discuss this article:
